correctness.rationale: For exact (m+1,1...) cluster the coefficient algebra is C[a,v²,v³]: the centered coefficients at orders two and three have nonzero constants for every m>=2, and all higher powers belong to that algebra; coprime analytic factorization adds smooth factors. For exact (m,m,1...) disjoint Hensel clusters identify the image with a reduced union of two independently straightened smooth power curves; the scheme ideal is the cross-product monomial ideal. The fiber-product exact sequence gives dimension q+m-1 and depth q+1 (for m=2 a hypersurface). Localization at the pair-root generic point has dimension m-1 and depth one; for m>=3 this violates S2. The accompanying package checker passes finite independent symbolic instances but is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The exact two-branch presentation yields a structural homological obstruction in all higher multiple-root loci m>=3,d>=2m: generic non-Cohen--Macaulayness with exact depth defect m-2 and a concrete failure of S2. This resolves a natural local singularity question for an infinite, classically motivated family and refines previously qualitative nodal/cuspidal stratification. The nontrivial conclusion is not a mere restatement of singular support or a finite example.
